question: While exploring music history, you come across two videos. One features a musician performing a cover of a well-known duet, and the other provides information on a vintage Gibson L48 guitar, including the year it was manufactured. Calculate the total number of days between January 1 of the guitar's manufacturing year and the official US single release date of the original song that is covered in the first video.
output:
**Analysis of the two videos:**

- **Video 1:** The singer performs the lyrics "You do something to me that I can't explain / Hold me closer and I feel no pain / Every beat of my heart, we got something going on / Tender love is blind, it requires a dedication..." — this is a cover of **"Islands in the Stream,"** the famous duet written by the Bee Gees and originally recorded by **Kenny Rogers & Dolly Parton**. Per Wikipedia, the official US single release date was **August 15, 1983** (from the album *Eyes That See in the Dark*, B-side "I Will Always Love You").

- **Video 2:** In the audio, Dan Erlewine states, "Here is a **1948** Gibson archtop guitar, model L-48" — so the manufacturing year is **1948**, giving a start date of **January 1, 1948**.

**Calculation (verified with Python):**
- Jan 1, 1948 → Jan 1, 1983: 35 years × 365 days + 9 leap days (1948–1980) = 12,784 days
- Jan 1, 1983 → Aug 15, 1983: 226 days
- Total: 12,784 + 226 = **13,010 days** (≈ 35.6 years)

<answer>13,010 days</answer>

"**Islands in the Stream**" is a song written by the [Bee Gees] and recorded by American [country music] artists [Kenny Rogers] and [Dolly Parton]. It was released in August 1983 as the first single from Rogers's fifteenth studio album _[Eyes That See in the Dark]_. The Bee Gees released a live version in 1998 and a studio version in 2001.

The song reached number one on the [_Billboard_ Hot 100] chart in the United States, giving each of Rogers and Parton their second pop number-one hit (after Rogers's "[Lady] "Lady (Kenny Rogers song)")" in 1980 and Parton's "[9 to 5] "9 to 5 (Dolly Parton song)")" in 1981). It also topped the Country and Adult Contemporary charts. In 2005, the song topped [Country Music Television]'s poll of the best country duets of all time; Parton and Rogers reunited to perform the song on a [CMT] "CMT (American TV channel)") special. As of May 2023, it has been triple [certified Platinum] by the [Recording Industry Association of America] for three million certified units.[[2]]#cite_note-ReferenceA-2)

Rogers and Parton went on to record a Christmas album together and had an additional hit with their 1985 duet "[Real Love] "Real Love (Dolly Parton and Kenny Rogers song)")".

## Background

[[edit]&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Background")]

Named after [the 1970 novel] "Islands in the Stream (novel)") by [Ernest Hemingway], the song was originally written for [Diana Ross] in an R&B style but later reworked for the duet by Rogers and Parton.[[3]]#cite_note-3)[[4]]#cite_note-BB-4)

It has been claimed that the song was also intended for [Marvin Gaye]. This is attributed to a 2001 _[Good Morning America]_ interview with the Bee Gees. When Barry Gibb said the song was written for Ross, Robin Gibb interrupted and said, "No, we wrote it for Marvin Gaye ... We sent it to him but he was dead so it was a bit difficult for him to sing it."[[5]]#cite_note-5)[[6]]#cite_note-6) Gaye actually died in 1984, a year after the recording.[[7]]#cite_note-7) Separately, Robin Gibb has said the song was stylistically written "... as a [Tamla] kind of soul song in a Marvin Gaye type feel", though not asserting it was for Gaye.[[8]]#cite_note-8) In other interviews, Barry Gibb has always maintained that Ross was the original artist for the song with no mention of Gaye.[[4]]#cite_note-BB-4)[[9]]#cite_note-9)

For licensing reasons, the song was not included on the digital release of _Eyes That See in the Dark_ from [Capitol Records Nashville]. [Sony Music], the current owner of [RCA Records], protected copyrights in the recording, which is digitally available only in various compilations from Sony Music, especially those of [Dolly Parton].

## Musical structure

[[edit]&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Musical structure")]

The song is sung in moderate [**4** **4** time], with Rogers and Parton alternating lead vocals. Their version is in [C major] when Rogers sings lead, but [changes] "Modulation (music)") to [A-flat major] when Parton takes over the lead.[[10]]#cite_note-10)

## Critical reception

[[edit]&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Critical reception")]

_[Cash Box]_ said that "the sound is simply gorgeous, as is the melody, as are the voices."[[11]]#cite_note-11)

In 2024, _[Rolling Stone]_ ranked the song at #104 on its 200 Greatest Country Songs of All Time ranking.[[12]]#cite_note-12)

## Commercial performance

[[edit]&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Commercial performance")]

The song knocked [Bonnie Tyler]'s "[Total Eclipse of the Heart]" out of No. 1 on the _Billboard_ Hot 100, also topping the Country and Adult Contemporary listings. In December of that year, it was [certified platinum] by the [Recording Industry Association of America] for selling over two million physical copies in the US.[[2]]#cite_note-ReferenceA-2) After becoming available for digital download, it had sold a further 834,000 digital copies in the US, as of January 2019[[update]]&action=edit).[[13]]#cite_note-13)

In Australia, the song was number one for one week in December 1983 and became one of the highest selling singles of 1984.

The song reached a peak of No. 7 in the UK Singles Chart in 1983. As of July 2014[[update]]&action=edit), it had also sold 245,577 digital copies in the UK.[[14]]#cite_note-14)As of 2017[[update]]&action=edit), it had racked up 287,200 downloads and 4.83 million streams in the UK.[[15]]#cite_note-15) "Islands in the Stream" reappeared on the UK Singles Chart at No. 13 after Parton's death in August 2026, with the [Official Charts Company] reporting the song had amassed 2,195,255 total units in the UK since 1994.[[16]]#cite_note-16)

## In popular media

[[edit]&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: In popular media")]

In April 2008, [South Bend], [Indiana], radio station [WZOW] played the song continuously for several days on end,[[17]]#cite_note-17) a [stunt] "Stunting (broadcasting)") drawing attention to the station's format change from [alternative rock] to [adult contemporary].

The song is prominently featured in the 2025 film, _[You're Cordially Invited]_, starring [Will Ferrell] and [Reese Witherspoon].

"**Islands in the Stream**" is a song written by the [Bee Gees] and recorded by American [country music] artists [Kenny Rogers] and [Dolly Parton]. It was released in August 1983 as the first single from Rogers's fifteenth studio album _[Eyes That See in the Dark]_. The Bee Gees released a live version in 1998 and a studio version in 2001.

The song reached number one on the [_Billboard_ Hot 100] chart in the United States, giving each of Rogers and Parton their second pop number-one hit (after Rogers's "[Lady] "Lady (Kenny Rogers song)")" in 1980 and Parton's "[9 to 5] "9 to 5 (Dolly Parton song)")" in 1981). It also topped the Country and Adult Contemporary charts. In 2005, the song topped [Country Music Television]'s poll of the best country duets of all time; Parton and Rogers reunited to perform the song on a [CMT] "CMT (American TV channel)") special. As of May 2023, it has been triple [certified Platinum] by the [Recording Industry Association of America] for three million certified units.[[2]]#cite_note-ReferenceA-2)

Rogers and Parton went on to record a Christmas album together and had an additional hit with their 1985 duet "[Real Love] "Real Love (Dolly Parton and Kenny Rogers song)")".

## Background

[[edit]&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Background")]

Named after [the 1970 novel] "Islands in the Stream (novel)") by [Ernest Hemingway], the song was originally written for [Diana Ross] in an R&B style but later reworked for the duet by Rogers and Parton.[[3]]#cite_note-3)[[4]]#cite_note-BB-4)

It has been claimed that the song was also intended for [Marvin Gaye]. This is attributed to a 2001 _[Good Morning America]_ interview with the Bee Gees. When Barry Gibb said the song was written for Ross, Robin Gibb interrupted and said, "No, we wrote it for Marvin Gaye ... We sent it to him but he was dead so it was a bit difficult for him to sing it."[[5]]#cite_note-5)[[6]]#cite_note-6) Gaye actually died in 1984, a year after the recording.[[7]]#cite_note-7) Separately, Robin Gibb has said the song was stylistically written "... as a [Tamla] kind of soul song in a Marvin Gaye type feel", though not asserting it was for Gaye.[[8]]#cite_note-8) In other interviews, Barry Gibb has always maintained that Ross was the original artist for the song with no mention of Gaye.[[4]]#cite_note-BB-4)[[9]]#cite_note-9)

For licensing reasons, the song was not included on the digital release of _Eyes That See in the Dark_ from [Capitol Records Nashville]. [Sony Music], the current owner of [RCA Records], protected copyrights in the recording, which is digitally available only in various compilations from Sony Music, especially those of [Dolly Parton].

## Musical structure

[[edit]&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Musical structure")]

The song is sung in moderate [**4** **4** time], with Rogers and Parton alternating lead vocals. Their version is in [C major] when Rogers sings lead, but [changes] "Modulation (music)") to [A-flat major] when Parton takes over the lead.[[10]]#cite_note-10)

## Critical reception

[[edit]&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Critical reception")]

_[Cash Box]_ said that "the sound is simply gorgeous, as is the melody, as are the voices."[[11]]#cite_note-11)

In 2024, _[Rolling Stone]_ ranked the song at #104 on its 200 Greatest Country Songs of All Time ranking.[[12]]#cite_note-12)

## Commercial performance

[[edit]&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Commercial performance")]

The song knocked [Bonnie Tyler]'s "[Total Eclipse of the Heart]" out of No. 1 on the _Billboard_ Hot 100, also topping the Country and Adult Contemporary listings. In December of that year, it was [certified platinum] by the [Recording Industry Association of America] for selling over two million physical copies in the US.[[2]]#cite_note-ReferenceA-2) After becoming available for digital download, it had sold a further 834,000 digital copies in the US, as of January 2019[[update]]&action=edit).[[13]]#cite_note-13)

In Australia, the song was number one for one week in December 1983 and became one of the highest selling singles of 1984.

The song reached a peak of No. 7 in the UK Singles Chart in 1983. As of July 2014[[update]]&action=edit), it had also sold 245,577 digital copies in the UK.[[14]]#cite_note-14)As of 2017[[update]]&action=edit), it had racked up 287,200 downloads and 4.83 million streams in the UK.[[15]]#cite_note-15) "Islands in the Stream" reappeared on the UK Singles Chart at No. 13 after Parton's death in August 2026, with the [Official Charts Company] reporting the song had amassed 2,195,255 total units in the UK since 1994.[[16]]#cite_note-16)

## In popular media

[[edit]&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: In popular media")]

In April 2008, [South Bend], [Indiana], radio station [WZOW] played the song continuously for several days on end,[[17]]#cite_note-17) a [stunt] "Stunting (broadcasting)") drawing attention to the station's format change from [alternative rock] to [adult contemporary].

The song is prominently featured in the 2025 film, _[You're Cordially Invited]_, starring [Will Ferrell] and [Reese Witherspoon].
